clue.text: Controller of players in club cricket side

parts.note: a cricket bat is a club for hitting the ball
the on side (leg side) is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: Someone in a cricket club team takes charge of the other players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Controller of players' looks like a team captain, but the players are musicians and the controller is the conductor's stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor uses this slender stick to direct an orchestra's musicians.

clue.text: Hunt initially moves up and down 'for winter sport

parts.note: to bob is to move up and down
Leigh is the first name of Leigh Hunt, the Romantic poet and essayist

explanation.surface: In a hunt, the first rider bobs up and down for some winter sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal, but it points to the first name of the writer Leigh Hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing a steerable sled down an ice track is a Winter Olympic event.

clue.text: Means to pick up lots of criminals out East

definitions.meaning: a gripping tool for lifting things such as coal
Chinese secret societies or criminal gangs

explanation.definitionFit: A gripping tool lifts things; the same word names Chinese criminal gangs.

clue.text: No veteran expected to achieve a clean sweep

definitions.text: No veteran expected to achieve a clean sweep

parts.words: No veteran expected to achieve a clean sweep
parts.note: a newly appointed person, not an old hand, who is expected to make sweeping changes, after the proverb about sweeping clean

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says a newcomer to office sweeps clean, making many reforms at once.

clue.text: Where one learned to adjust without mother

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: to adjust something is to alter it
mama is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the place where they learned to cope without their mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' suggests leaving mother out, but it is used in its old sense of outside, so mother sits within the word for adjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'nourishing mother', the phrase names the school or university a person attended.

clue.text: Bark of a golden retriever?

parts.note: bark means a ship, and the golden retriever is Jason, who fetched the Golden Fleece in his vessel

explanation.definitionFit: Jason sailed this ship to recover the Golden Fleece in Greek myth.

clue.text: Political group replacing column by ad

indicators.note: replacing means putting letters back in a different place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political party swaps a newspaper column for an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: The MONDAY CLUB is a right-wing British Conservative pressure group.
explanation.definitionFit: This British organisation is a right-wing pressure group tied to the Conservative Party.

clue.text: Crazy artistic set in a city out East

parts.note: mad means crazy
RAs are Royal Academicians, members of an artistic body

explanation.surface: A wild crowd of artists gathers in an Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian city, now called Chennai, lies on the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Follow clubs, perhaps, in sporting outfit

parts.note: to track someone is to follow them
clubs is one suit in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A golfer follows their clubs around in sportswear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests golf, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletes wear this loose two-piece garment while training.

clue.text: Sequence of shots bringing recovery

definitions.meaning: an exchange of strokes in tennis or squash
a revival, as in prices that pick up

explanation.definitionFit: It is a long exchange in tennis and also a rebound in markets or health.

clue.text: Ring: comedian about vehicle for musicians

parts.note: a band is a ring, as in a wedding band
a wag is a joker or wit
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A comic hangs around a wrestling ring near a musicians' van.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the wagon carrying a parade's band, the word now means a popular movement people join.

clue.text: Tow-line, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: to draw a load is to tow it

explanation.surface: A tow-line is described in some particular way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'Tow-line' looks like one rope but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow lengthened way of talking is a recognisable speech style.

clue.text: What's attractive about stone?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a lure is something that attracts
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A question about why polished stone appeals to people.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: a stone's sheen is what attracts. ST is stone, a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The gleam or sheen of a polished gem is exactly what makes it attractive.

clue.text: Cheeky clue?..Nonsense!

parts.note: malar is the anatomical adjective for the cheek, as in the malar bone
a key is a clue to a puzzle

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an impudent crossword clue as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheeky' reads as impudent, but here it is literally 'of the cheek', the anatomical adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal exclamation for rubbish or humbug talk.

clue.text: Assisting priest without cent? Something wrong there

indicators.note: without means outside, so one piece is put around another

parts.note: in a curacy describes serving as a curate, an assistant priest

explanation.surface: An assistant priest finds himself penniless and wonders what went wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' seems to mean lacking the cent, but it means outside it: IN A CURACY goes around C.
explanation.definitionFit: An error or mistake is something wrong, a failure to be correct.

clue.text: Well punished by benign penal system?

definitions.meaning: read literally, being held in a kindly prison, nick being slang for jail

explanation.surface: A healthy prisoner credits a lenient jail.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is British slang for a prison or police station, so the phrase whimsically means detained in a kindly jail.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in sound condition, healthy or working properly.

clue.text: Thousands of pounds beat the highest bid

parts.note: grand is slang for a thousand pounds
to slam is to beat or hit hard

explanation.surface: Thousands of pounds outbid every rival at an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, bidding all thirteen tricks is the top contract, the highest possible bid.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, contracting to win all thirteen tricks is the top call one can make.

clue.text: Outstanding example of modern opera

definitions.meaning: a remarkable person or thing, a humdinger
Alban Berg's twentieth-century opera of that title

explanation.definitionFit: Informally a remarkable specimen is a humdinger, and Berg's 1937 opera bears the same name.

clue.text: Special fund I need not handled by harmless drudge?

indicators.note: special here signals an unusual arrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A charity appeal says a special fund is needed for dull work.
explanation.walkthrough: Samuel Johnson defined a lexicographer as 'a harmless drudge', so a word he did not handle is one not given a meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A word left out of the dictionary has no stated meaning, lacking clear explanation.

clue.text: Dismiss carriage that's not built safely

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse carriage

explanation.surface: A coachman sacks a builder whose carriage is unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: A building with poor escape routes is dangerously flammable and unsafe.

clue.text: Act as judge in this case, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals that the word is spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: here means in this case or in this instance

explanation.surface: A lawyer asks someone to be the judge in this particular trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests a court case, which keeps the legal picture going.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge hears a case, listening to it and trying it in court.

clue.text: Familiar account whimsical editor shortened

parts.note: quaint means oddly old-fashioned or whimsical
ED is the shortened form of editor

explanation.surface: A whimsical editor cuts down a familiar story.
explanation.definitionFit: Being familiar with something means knowing it, having become versed in it.

clue.text: Secret things revealed in ear can astonish

indicators.note: revealed in shows the letters are exposed within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Secrets whispered in an ear can amaze the listener.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysteries or arcane knowledge are secret things known only to initiates.

clue.text: Charge less than others for some beef

definitions.meaning: the tenderloin cut from beneath the sirloin

explanation.definitionFit: Underselling rivals is one sense; it is also a butcher's name for the tenderloin cut.

clue.text: Not satisfied with menu, switched restaurant finally

indicators.note: switched means the letters are swapped around
finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A diner unhappy with the menu changed restaurant in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmet need or demand is one left unfulfilled.

clue.text: Live with 50% interest

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
fifty percent is a half

explanation.surface: Someone lives on investments earning fifty percent interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' suggests money, but here it means benefit, as in acting on someone's behalf.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting on someone's part means in their interest or for their benefit.

clue.text: One thing wanting in expression of regret

parts.note: A means one
a lack is something wanting or missing

explanation.surface: One thing missing prompts a sigh of regret.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic interjection, it expresses sorrow, like alas.

clue.text: Mark left on surface of rock formation

definitions.meaning: the mark a healed wound leaves on the skin
a steep rocky cliff face on a hillside

explanation.definitionFit: A healed wound leaves a mark; in northern England the word also names a craggy cliff.

clue.text: Island's whisky, first-class

parts.note: malt is a type of whisky
A, as in A1 or grade A, means first-class

explanation.surface: An island boasts that its whisky is top quality.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mediterranean island nation lies south of Sicily.

clue.text: Become aware of new Cartesian order

indicators.note: new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters
order reinforces the rearranging, asking for the letters in a different sequence

explanation.surface: A philosopher discovers a new order of Descartes' thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' and 'order' together ask for one fresh arrangement of the letters of CARTESIAN, the adjective from the philosopher Descartes.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out for certain is to come to know a fact, making sure of it.

clue.text: Novel hero we may, sort out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A novel's hero says we may sort things out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort' looks like the instruction to rearrange, but it is part of the letters; 'out' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain's boyish title character is the hero of an American novel.

clue.text: Created incitement, .sanctioned after pressure

indicators.note: after means the following piece comes later, placed behind

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
to OK something is to approve it, so sanctioned gives OKED

explanation.surface: Agitation was stirred up once pressure brought official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod someone into action, metaphorically, is to incite or stir them up.
